post.caption: Cubic zirconia came from a laser lab. Scientists at the Lebedev Physical Institute in Moscow developed it while looking for a crystal to use in lasers, and the team published its growing method in 1973. In Russia, it is called fianit, after the institute's abbreviation, FIAN. Radio waves melt the zirconia inside a water-cooled container, and a solid crust called the skull forms around the melt. Zirconia melts at about 2,700 degrees Celsius. Colorless stones reached the jewelry market in 1976. It rates about 8 on the Mohs scale, and diamond rates 10. A CZ weighs about 1.7 times as much as a same-size diamond.
